old: They sprinkle their horses like racers in the contests; they hasten with the ears of the roaring one, with the swift ones. Gold-helmeted Maruts, shaking, of one fury, you go to nourishment with the spotted mares.

why: reviewer (minor): 'their' is not in the text (aśvān atyān iva only); Hindi has no possessive either.

old: For nourishment all these beings have grown strong, or for Mitra always, O you of swift gifts. With spotted horses, of unfailing bounty, like straight-going ones seated at the pole on the ways.

why: reviewer (minor): bhuvana is rendered 'world' in 2.33.9 (bhuvanasya 'of this ... world'); 'beings' makes the group inconsistent.
